label: weak copy-phase unit on specific echoed tokens (n,u,p,w,q,k,2), mid recall positions
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L; never on original or delimiter steps), mostly at recall_idx 2-4 (about 85% of mass) with a smaller bump at recall_idx 7-8 in long sequences, and never at recall_idx 0-1. Input-token preference: n, u, p, w, q, k, 2 (n alone holds ~30% of mass); also mild preferences for prev_tok q/g and out_tok 2/n/g/l. Activations are tiny (max 0.003 above threshold). The predicate (copy phase, recall 2-4, in_tok in that set) covers ~80% of activation mass but has ~4% precision; adding prev_tok/out_tok sets only reaches F1 ~0.24. No coherent rule separates active steps from the many inactive steps with the same tokens and positions, so this is a sparse conjunction of token identities, not an interpretable feature. Magnitude modulators were not established.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: n, u, p, w, q, k; least: 1, e, j, 3) and the previous input (most: q, g, n, 2, p, l; least: 0, f, h, d); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, L=4 & t=6, L=7 & t=10.
